name: repo-fit
description: Give your project a memory: a session briefing, one list of everything open, safe automatic saves and one rulebook for Claude Code and Codex. Works on new and existing projects.
author: Jimmy Sadek

releases.why: Deep mode: repo-fit can now look inside your folders and, after one yes, put every document in its place on a separate branch, one proven step at a time, without touching your folder.
releases.briefing: repo-fit 0.9.0: ask for a deep pass, and your documents, specs and rulebook get sorted on a separate branch you merge when happy.
news: Deep sweep 1: one docs/ folder by kind, a status line on every spec and plan, copies to the archive, and a shorter rulebook with every rule kept word for word.
Every change goes on a new branch made in a separate working copy, one commit per step. Your folder, your branch and your files stay as they are until you merge.
Each step is proven before the next: no file lost, no link broken, every rule kept, and your folder's own check still passes. A step that fails is taken back and named.

Deep sweep 2 for code: after you read the plan and say yes, unused code goes, files get names that say what they hold, and colours and spacing move to one place, each step proven by your own tests and build.
A folder set up for Codex only before 0.7.3 gets the CLAUDE.md it was missing from update.

releases.why: Safety and privacy: the snapshot before a change stays off your branches, private folders stay out of Git and out of the map, and the map no longer copies your open tasks.
releases.briefing: repo-fit 0.8.0: the safety snapshot now stays off your branches, and MAP.md shows only how many open tasks there are, not their words.
news: The safety snapshot before a change is now kept apart from your branches: your branch, what you staged and your files stay exactly as they are, and a normal git push does not send it.
Before it saves anything, the screen names the files it will save and warns about private folders (meeting notes, customers) that are not kept out of Git, with one command to keep them out.
Files Git ignores never reach the map, the index pages, the open-work count or the checkup.
MAP.md shows only how many open tasks there are. node scripts/playbook/map.mjs --open lists them on screen.
When MAP.md is kept out of Git, the rules point new sessions at README.md instead, and the checkup says so.
The checkup says what it does not check, and a change to the rules names your other working copies, which keep the old rules until they take it.

releases.why: Small fixes: a new setup always gets a CLAUDE.md next to AGENTS.md, Git is never started without its own yes, and the update line names every way to update.
releases.briefing: New: repo-fit can organize your folder. Ask your assistant to run /repo-fit to see the plan. Nothing changes without your yes.
news: A new setup now always gets a short CLAUDE.md next to AGENTS.md, so Claude Code reads the same rules, also when you set up for Codex only. A folder you set up before does not get one from update.
In a folder without Git, repo-fit changes nothing until you choose: start Git and save a snapshot first (recommended), or go on with repo-fit's own backup and undo.
The line about a newer repo-fit names every way to update: npx skills update, skillshare update --all, git pull in its folder, or /plugin in Claude Code.

releases.why: Fixes from the first real sessions: a website's own folders get no index page, archived copies no longer show as broken links or open work, and the briefing can come without the end-of-reply reminder.
releases.briefing: New: repo-fit can organize your folder. Ask your assistant to run /repo-fit to see the plan. Nothing changes without your yes.
news: In a folder that is a website or an app, its own folders (content, src, public and similar) get no index page; the map links the folder itself.
Archived copies of other projects in outputs/ or archive/ are no longer checked for broken links or counted as open work.
`hooks --hooks briefing` turns on the briefing without the end-of-reply reminder, and repo-fit remembers that choice.
The safety snapshot leaves tool clutter out (.serena/, caches).

releases.why: Fixes from the first upgrade of a real folder: nothing is written into a folder that never chose a map, secret notes stay private, template copies stay where their program needs them.
releases.briefing: New: repo-fit can organize your folder. Ask your assistant to run /repo-fit to see the plan. Nothing changes without your yes.
news: A folder that never chose a map gets none: the session start only updates a map you said yes to.
A note whose name says secret or private is listed by its name only; its words never reach a page.
Files with the same name in parallel folders (copies of a template) stay where they are; only a file named like a copy goes to the archive.
Pictures linked from a book's own folder count as working links, and a template's placeholders are not reported as broken.
Undo now also puts back an older .playbook/.gitignore, and the safety snapshot never saves repo-fit's own records.

releases.why: repo-fit can now organize your folder: it shows the folder before and after, asks once, and keeps it organized. Nothing is deleted, and one command undoes it.
releases.briefing: New: repo-fit can organize your folder. Ask your assistant to run /repo-fit to see the plan. Nothing changes without your yes.
news: A map of your folder (MAP.md) and an index page per folder, so you and your assistant find any note in two steps.
Organize with one yes: loose files go into folders, old folders and exact copies go to an archive, and the screen shows before, after and why first. Nothing is deleted; one command undoes it.
Before any change, Git saves a snapshot of your folder, so you can always go back. A folder without Git gets Git started first (since 0.7.3, only after its own yes).
New things go in inbox/ and are filed by the rules you approved, when a session starts.
The briefing names real problems in one short line each and stays quiet otherwise. Running /repo-fit again starts with a checkup.
Open tasks from all your notes are listed in one place, in MAP.md.

releases.why: Setup now asks you once instead of a dozen times, and the shared rules in AGENTS.md shrink to 293 words that never override yours.
news: The shared rules in AGENTS.md shrink from 774 to 293 words. They go after your own rules and say yours win where they overlap. No more rules about branches, when to commit, or board columns.
The briefing no longer says "never commit on main". Without a board, it shows your last three commits instead of an error.
A long list of unlinked notes in the briefing becomes a count, with one command that lists them.
You turn the start-of-session briefing on yourself with one line, because Claude Code does not let an assistant change how sessions start.

A reminder at the end of each reply: when files changed but nothing was written down, the assistant is asked once whether anything is worth keeping. It never pushes you to save; your rules decide that. Turn it on with the same one line as the briefing.

steps.D-01: The shared rules block is now 293 words, goes after your rules, and your rules win where they overlap. It no longer needs a table board or sets branch and commit rules.
